title: Cost Control Matrix & Lane Rollup — map workload patterns to batching, cache, and quant profiles
creator: Priya Desai
description:
This initiative builds a pragmatic "cost control matrix" and lane rollup that maps common customer workload patterns (short-chat, long-form generation, embedding-heavy, streaming interactive) to a small set of validated inference configurations: batching knobs, KV-cache TTL policies, and quantization profiles. The goal is to make conservative, empirically-backed recommendations surfaced in the Console and API docs so product/platform teams can reduce unit cost without unexpected quality regressions.

Scope:
- Define workload taxonomy and signals (token distribution, request concurrency, latency sensitivity).
- Produce a matrix that maps each workload lane to 1) default batch size policy, 2) KV-cache strategy (prefix TTL, shard rules), 3) quant profile suggestion (FP16/int8/FP32 fallback strategy), 4) routing tier recommendation.
- Implement a lane-rollup view in Console that shows per-route recommended knobs, estimated cost delta, and safety checks.
- Create experiment harness and automated evals (quality delta thresholds) for each recommended quant profile.
- Run field experiments on a subset of Dedicated customers and opt-in hosted routes to validate real-world savings and monitor regressions.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing model selection or full autotune engine in this phase. This is a recommendation/ramp plan and observability surface, not an automatic operator that changes customer configs without consent.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Matrix covers >=5 workload lanes with concrete example routes and measured baselines (latency, p50/p99, token-cost)
A2: Console lane-rollup UI prototype shows recommended knobs, estimated per-token savings, and links to experiment results
A3: Automated evals produce quality delta reports for quant profiles with configurable guardrail thresholds
A4: Field trials demonstrate >=12% median cost reduction on opt-in routes with <2% measured quality drift (or an approved mitigation plan)
A5: Runbook and rollout checklist published (docs + PR template + rollback criteria)
milestones: M1: Workload taxonomy and baseline collection (2026-03-07)
M3: Console UI prototype and API surface (2026-03-28)
M4: Eval harness + quant regression guardrails (2026-04-04)
M6: Rollout report and OKR sign-off (2026-04-15)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization; mitigated by per-prompt eval sets and automatic fallback to higher-precision profile
Overfitting the matrix to internal workloads; mitigate by including partner/customer examples and telemetry sampling
Console surface may create support load; include contextual help and opt-in toggles to reduce friction
implementation_notes: Telemetry: Add lightweight tagging on routes for lane classification — ensure tags are sampled and privacy-friendly
